title: Personal Checking: Combined Deposit Balance for a Private Client Checking Conversion
content:
## What this balance is for

The Private Client Checking entry gate, when it is applied to the conversion of an existing Personal Checking account, is tested against a combined deposit balance defined for that purpose alone. This page sets out the date it refers to, what its account part carries, and the holdings it sums.

## Moment of measurement

The balance refers to the date on which the conversion request is dealt with. Its first part is the converting account's own ledger balance, and for this test that ledger balance is the one that carries every credit the bank already owes the account. Only posted entries make up a ledger balance; a pending credit makes up none of it.

What the bank already owes, for this purpose, covers two kinds of credit. One is a fee refund owed on the bank-error ground, or owed as the refund that follows a dispute decided for the owner, whichever fee it concerns and whichever rule establishes it. The other is a provisional credit that has fallen due on a dispute in submitted status, however its amount is worked out. A courtesy refund never belongs here, since it is a goodwill gesture granted only on request.

## Parts of the balance

The balance is the sum of:

1. **This checking account** — its posted ledger balance, taken as zero if it is negative.
2. **Savings** — what the owner's savings account in applied status currently holds, together with the one in active status and the one in dormant status.
3. **Certificates of deposit** — the principal of the owner's certificate in applied status, of the one in active status and of the one in grace period status.
4. **Mortgage** — yes, it counts: Private Client Checking takes mortgage principal into account, so the principal of the owner's mortgage loan in active status, of the one in delinquent status and of the one in forbearance status is added.

Not counted: the owner's other checking accounts. Where the owner has several savings accounts, certificates or mortgage loans sharing one status, only the first of them on the customer's record enters the sum. Figures for these holdings are taken from the owner's records under Savings & Money Market Accounts, Certificates of Deposit and Home Mortgage Loans respectively.

## Worked sum (hypothetical holdings)

| Holding | Status | Amount (USD) | Counted |
|---|---|---|---|
| this checking account | active | 12500.00 | 12500.00 |
| second checking account | active | 30000.00 | not counted |
| savings account | active | 64000.00 | 64000.00 |
| certificate | grace period | 40000.00 | 40000.00 |
| certificate | closed | 25000.00 | not counted |
| mortgage loan | delinquent | 118000.00 | 118000.00 |

Combined deposit balance: 12500.00 plus 64000.00 plus 40000.00 plus 118000.00, which is 234500.00 USD. Were this checking account overdrawn, its part would be zero and the sum 222000.00 USD.
